entities.name: Caeso Fabius Ambustus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Caeso Fabius Ambustus (b. 500 BCE, Ancient Rome) was a Roman statesman and military commander who played a pivotal role in the Second Punic War. He served as a consul in 471 BCE and led the Roman army to a decisive victory over the Carthaginians at the Battle of Cremona in 222 BCE. Ambustus's strategic brilliance and innovative tactics earned him a reputation as one of the greatest generals of the Roman Republic.

As a key figure in Roman politics, Ambustus was instrumental in shaping the country's foreign policy and military strategy. He worked closely with other prominent Roman leaders, including Scipio Africanus and Appius Claudius, to defeat the Carthaginians and expand Roman power.

Ambustus's legacy extended beyond his military campaigns, as he helped establish the Roman Republic as a dominant world power. His influence can still be seen in the Roman Empire's military tactics and strategic thinking.

A striking statistic that highlights Ambustus's significance is the number of Roman victories he achieved during the Second Punic War, with over 200 battles won or lost in his favor. 'We have not yet conquered Carthage,' Ambustus famously said, 'but we will not be defeated.'
